notes: Three-form player character. Forms A/B share one mesh+skeleton (visual-only delta). Form C is a separate mesh+superset skeleton. See design/requirements.md for the locked numbers this plan builds to. task-config.json now exists (character task): symmetry=mirror_left (default), rig=biped_ik (default), correctives=true (default).

components.label: Form A — human base mesh (hard-mirrored, retopo'd, verified)
components.description: REBUILT 2026-09-18 as the definitive Form A. Hard-mirrored the ALREADY-retopo'd wip-8 mesh via the measured-midplane-aware symmetrize_mesh(keep='+X') function directly (a true split-and-flip, not the tolerance-gated wrapper) -- residual went from 21.29mm to exactly 0.000mm. Decimate (needed to stay near the 15k budget) is not mirror-aware and reintroduced 0.395mm; re-mirrored a second time AFTER decimate and did not touch face count again, landing at 15558 faces (1.04x budget, accepted). Re-unwrapped UVs each time symmetry was rewritten (both generate_3d's own UV pass and retopo's internal UV pass silently add layers that block a real rewrite -- strip uv_layers before every hard-mirror call). Saved as models/werewolf-wip-9.blend.
components.technique_note: task-config.json's symmetry=mirror_left is NOT wired into rigforge_landmarks.py as of this session (grepped the file -- no task_config/mirror_left/as_designed references at all). Calling rigforge_landmarks(action='prepare') still uses the OLD tolerance-gated logic (skips the rewrite if measured asymmetry is already under the 0.5mm SYMMETRY_TOLERANCE_MM, which is exactly the 'snap' bug the config mode was meant to replace). To get a guaranteed exact 0.000mm hard mirror, call rigforge_landmarks.measure_symmetry() + rigforge_landmarks.symmetrize_mesh(obj, midplane, keep='+X') directly via the module (bypassing prepare_for_rigging's tolerance gate) -- this is what actually worked. Worth fixing at the tool level in a future pass so 'hard-mirror' doesn't require reaching around the wrapper.

components.label: Form A/B — shared biped skeleton
components.description: Re-rigged through the landmark path with fresh auto-tags (UniRig detector, FORGE_RIGBRIDGE env var required -- see prior session's note, still needed here). fit_method='landmarks', zero warnings on the successful call. IK convention (legs IK, arms FK), correctives (8 JCMs, knee.L/R + elbow.L/R), and the walk cycle were re-authored fresh on the new joints.

echo_renders.honest_read: Confirmed: arms run down the sleeve centerline, legs and spine centered, both views clean by eye.

weight_maps_2026_09_18.honest_read: Both maps are clean and tightly localized to their own limb with a smooth falloff -- no visible leakage onto the torso or adjacent limb in either image. This does NOT show the breast<->pelvis overlap finding below, since neither breast nor pelvis was one of the two bones rendered.

tag_constrained_skinning_2026_09_18.finding: Ran (confirmed via direct rigforge_skin(action='apply') call, which matched the auto-embedded result almost exactly) but did NOT reach 0.000 overlap on this character, contrary to the commit message's 'werewolf: stray 4.351->0.000' example. Measured: stray_mass 91.86, verdict fail, 8 outlier pairs, worst = 320 vertices shared between DEF-breast.L and DEF-pelvis.R (382mm apart).
tag_constrained_skinning_2026_09_18.root_cause: Tag-constrained skinning only blocks CROSS-tag weight leakage. This character's 'Torso' tag is one bucket covering 13 bones (both breast bones, both pelvis bones, and the full spine chain) -- breast and pelvis are BOTH legal for any Torso-tagged vertex, so bone-heat weight bleeding between them (they are anatomically 382mm apart but topologically close across a thin jacket+jeans mesh) is allowed by the rule and untouched by the constraint. This is a real, reproducible measurement, not a bug in how the tool was called -- re-running rigforge_skin directly reproduced the same number. A finer tag split (e.g. separate Chest/Pelvis tags within Torso) would likely fix it but was not attempted this round -- it is a bigger tagging change than 'apply the new default'.
tag_constrained_skinning_2026_09_18.reported_honestly: The artist was told the real number (91.86, not 0.000) rather than the commit's example, with the mechanism explained.

continuity_2026_09_18.worst: DEF-foot.R: 0.00 weight at one vertex while neighbours average 0.92
continuity_2026_09_18.note: New fifth gate this session. 32 of 35 bone regions show at least one small weight hole; none reach the 'fail' band.

rig_check_2026_09_18_full.gate: FAIL overall (every joint still fails the intersections sub-gate at extreme poses -- same clothing-fabric-contact read as last session)
rig_check_2026_09_18_full.note_on_rest_intersections: Up from 220 last session. Not investigated further this round -- worth a look before Form B if it matters, but likely reflects the fresh regeneration+remirror rather than a regression in the rig itself.

centering.verdict: attention (no bone fails outright this time)
centering.worst: DEF-thigh.L.001 / DEF-thigh.R.001, 38.6mm, 54.1% of radius (both sides identical, as expected from the exact mirror)
centering.note: Real, measured improvement from last session's worst (63.8% fail, DEF-upper_arm.R) -- no bone fails outright now, matching the ballpark of the commit's own '58->36mm' example (we measured 38.6mm).

overlap.note: See tag_constrained_skinning_2026_09_18 above for the honest explanation -- this is worse than last session's 4.35, not better, and the cause is understood.

rig_check_2026_09_18_full.note_on_volume: Only knee/elbow fail volume now (both around 24-29%); everything else passes outright, including hip which had new-clips-only failures before. Correctives are doing real work: knee 070deg baseline is now 2.6% before correctives, 0.5% after.

known_issues: Overlap is genuinely worse than last session (91.86 vs 4.35) despite tag-constrained skinning running correctly -- root cause understood (Torso tag too coarse, see above), not yet fixed. A finer Torso tag split is the next concrete step if overlap needs to reach near-zero before Form B.
Centering improved to 'attention' everywhere (no outright fails) but nothing is fully 'ok' above the shin/forearm-tip bones -- real progress, not clean.
rest_intersections rose to 608 from 220 -- not investigated, flagged for a future look.

The task-config symmetry=mirror_left setting is not actually read by rigforge_landmarks yet -- the hard mirror this session was done by calling the underlying function directly. See form-a-human-base's technique_note.

history.note: materialised the character chain over an existing plan — 10 stages, all pending; 8 components already on the plan were left exactly as they were

stages.title: Reference — the pictures the build is measured against
stages.does: File the artist's references under design/refs/ and read them back in words they can correct. Nothing is generated from a picture nobody agreed was the picture.

stages.title: Design — requirements, concept diagram, settings sheet, sign-off
stages.does: The design phase: at most five questions in one message, then requirements.md, a hand-written concept.svg and the task-config sheet materialised at its defaults. Ends at the artist's yes.

stages.title: Generate — the base mesh exists
stages.does: A mesh in the scene, however rough. Judged on existence and watertightness only: shape is the next stage's problem and beauty is the artist's.

stages.title: Clean — symmetrize, retopo, bake, unwrap
stages.does: The finishing chain in its one correct order: repair, symmetrize to the task-config setting, retopo, UV unwrap, bake high->low, LODs. Every step after this one reads the atlas this one wrote.

stages.title: Correctives — the collapsed knee, fixed with a number
stages.does: A corrective shape key per bent joint, driven by bend angle. The fix ladder is law: correctives first quoting before/after, weight painting second, never a blind density pass (50.3% -> 51.1%).

stages.title: Export — the .glb the engine actually loads
stages.does: Baked deform rig, LOD chain sharing one atlas, correctives baked from their drivers into morph animation. glTF has no concept of a driver, so an unbaked morph reaches the engine pinned at zero, silently.
